record.what_it_does: Asana is a work/project management platform where teams organize, track, and manage tasks, projects, and workflows.
record.auth_notes: Personal access tokens (PATs) are static, long-lived bearer tokens generated instantly in the developer console and are the quickest way to authenticate. OAuth2 (authorization code grant, with PKCE support) is recommended when an app needs to support multiple users signing in. Service Accounts are an additional long-lived token type but are an Enterprise-tier feature that can only be created by an org's super admin (classified here as 'Other'). OpenID Connect is also offered on top of OAuth2 for login/identity use cases.
record.access_notes: Any developer can create a free Asana account, generate a PAT immediately from the developer console, and register an OAuth app (client ID/secret) with no cost or vendor approval. Approval/review is only required if the developer later chooses to publish the app publicly in Asana's App Directory (via 'Submit for review'); private/production OAuth distribution to any workspace does not require review.
